messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the DP kernel compile landed last night I am seeing sustained 99th latency spikes on model-raven; traffic slowly slipped into soft-429s around 02:10 UTC.
jamal: on it. is this the kernel switch you rolled earlier? which machine pool? :eyes: 
maria: yep, raven-dp v2 -> raven-dp-v2a (kernel 0x7c). Affected pool: dedicated-gpu-8a. KV-cache hit rates dropped from 78% -> 41% around the same time.
lee: kv hit drop is suspicious. Did the new kernel change KV eviction or prefetch semantics? any perf regressions in local bench? 
maria: local benches showed slightly higher throughput but the p99 increased on long sequences. Attached quick profiling extract:
```
profile: model-raven v2a
seq_len=1024
batch_assembly: avg=12ms -> 15ms (increase)
kv_get: avg=0.9ms -> 2.8ms
token_gen: avg=7.1ms -> 7.3ms
batch_size median: 6 -> 4
```
alex: batch_size shrinking + kv_get slower = more small batches hitting kernel overhead -> p99 jump. Any queue admission logs? 
maria: yes — queue admitted more small requests during prefetch drought. Admission controller shows token_budget target at 120 tokens / second but effective token burn spiked when KV misses rose.
jamal: snapshot of admission counters:
```
admit_window: 50ms
token_budget_target: 120
admitted_count: +18% (small batches)
soft_rejects: increased 4x
429_count: increased
kv_miss_rate: 59%
```
lee: ok, hypothesis: kernel changed memory layout so KV prefetch less effective, causing KV miss spike. That in turn reduces coalescing and shrinks batches. Our current admission policy tolerates more small batches rather than soft-shedding them -> compounding load.
alex: proposed mitigations:
- temporarily lower token_budget_target to 80 to force coalescing
- enable probabilistic small-batch soft-shed (p=0.6) for requests < 12 tokens
- tweak kernel selection fallback to prefer older kernel for seq_len>512 until kv fix
maria: tried lowering token_budget to 85 on a canary pool; results over 20m: p99 dropped 18%, kv miss rate unchanged (still high) but batch median rose to 5. soft-429s decreased.
jamal: can we add a fast metric to detect 'kv-induced batch fragmentation' — e.g., ratio small_batches / total_batches > 0.25 AND kv_miss_rate>50% -> trigger conservative admission.
lee: yes — we can add admission rule: if fragmentation and kv_miss high, reduce admit probability for small requests and increase prefetch aggressiveness (prefetch factor +1).
ci-bot: deploy status: rollout to canary pool completed at 4512340200. No failed tasks.
alex: longer-term: root fix is kernel kv behavior. Ops: roll back kernel on Dedicated 8a if kv_miss persists past 2 hours. Engineering: reproduce kv miss locally with same memory layout. Product: notify impacted customers if SLA risk.
maria: action items:
- jamal: implement admission rule quick patch (probabilistic soft-shed + token_budget override) — T+1h
- lee: reproduce kv miss with kernel instrumentation and open bug — T+6h
- alex: prepare rollback playbook and watch dashboard alerts — T+30m
- i'll monitor canary, post another update in ~30m
alex: ack. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
maria: update 30m later: canary p99 holding lower after token_budget change, but KV miss still elevated. Lee already found a memory alignment change in kernel 0x7c that affects prefetch stride. Investigating patch.
lee: extracted trace: prefetch stride was rounded from 64->128, causing fewer cachelines per prefetch on our key layout. sending patch now.
jamal: admission PR up: small-batch soft-shed + token_budget override. rolling to canary.
ci-bot: PR merged and canary deploy started.
alex: good. once kernel patch lands we'll test final rollback decision. 
maria: thanks — will update thread after kernel test. :rocket:
